To free from this pull, energy is to be supplied externally. 7.12 Geostationary Satellite Activity 7.3 Observe the activities that follow: i) Step out of your home, gaze up at the sky, and then take a telescope to focus your attention on a star positioned just above the zenith in the evening. ii) Get up precisely at around midnight, and observe the same star again, noting its position as before. iii) Repeat the same observation in the early morning and note the position of the star. iv) Repeat the same observation in the early morning and note the position of the star. Do the same activity around noon (you may find it hard to see the star) and note the position of the star. Q: i) Where will be the position of the star in each of the case? What was the resultant motion of the star during this period of observation? The star you observe consistently appears directly above the zenith. The Earth completes a cycle in a total time of 24 hours. The fact that the star maintains the same position every 24 hours indicates that it follows the same motion as the Earth, with the same time period. This makes the star appear stationary when viewed from the Earth. Therefore, in each instance, you perceive the star as if it were at rest, akin to a car in a park, and hence the name given to the orbit as a parking orbit or the geostationary orbit. A geostationary orbit or a parking orbit has the same time period as that of the Earth and is known as a synchronous orbit with T = 24 hours. A satellite revolving in such a parking orbit with T = 24 hours is called a geostationary satellite or a synchronous satellite. Such satellites are used in telecommunications, weather forecasting, and live video transmission from one part of the Earth to another.

Concept to know: The rotation of the Earth on its axis is from west to east. When we launch a satellite from west to east, the two velocities (linear velocities) are added to each other, enhancing the launching velocity of the rocket. In the equatorial plane, there is a high value of the linear velocity of the Earth that adds to the launching velocity of the satellite, making the launch more effective.
* When a body experiences zero weight, it is termed weightlessness. When a body falls under the effect of gravity without external resistance, it is referred to as free fall.
* Weightlessness is the effect of the free fall while the free fall is the cause of weightlessness.

The orbiting spacecraft is in the gravitational field of the Earth that experiences an appreciable weight and hence it is not in zero gravity though the case of weightlessness. 7.13 Global Positioning System (GPS)

Satellite-based navigation is utilized to synchronize location, velocity, and time while traveling by air, sea, or land. Similar fields that utilize GPS include military operations, surveying, aviation, road transportation, and smartphones.

The GPS, or Global Positioning System, is a global navigation satellite system consisting of a receiver and a constellation of 24 satellites distributed across six Earth-centered orbital planes, Physics, Grade 11 | 175
